about: Proposed region definitions for detailed maps outside the United States: Ontario, British Columbia and Guyana. A proposal for discussion (docs/REGIONS.md); no code reads this file, and it does not ship.

codes.proposal: ISO 3166-2 style codes: CA-ON, CA-BC, and GY for the whole country.
codes.why: Two-letter codes are what US state maps use, and CA already means California there (STATE_CODES and NAMES in the code, Lastbook-Map-CA.zip, derived/geo/addresses/CA.sqlite). ON, BC and GY do not collide with a US code, but a bare CA for Canada would.
codes.verified: The ISO 3166-2 codes were not checked against the ISO site in this change.

layer_keys.crops: crops.sqlite (crop types, or land cover where no crop map exists)

OGL-Canada.name: Open Government Licence – Canada 2.0
OGL-Canada.attribution: Use the provider's own attribution statement; if none, or if several providers make that impractical: "Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada."

OGL-Ontario.name: Open Government Licence – Ontario 1.0
OGL-Ontario.attribution: "Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Ontario." (or the provider's own statement)

OGL-BC.attribution: "Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – British Columbia." (or the provider's own statement). Applies only to BC Data Catalogue records that name it.

StatCan-Open.name: Statistics Canada Open Licence
StatCan-Open.attribution: For adapted data: "Adapted from Statistics Canada, <product>, <reference date>. This does not constitute an endorsement by Statistics Canada of this product."

ODbL-1.0.name: Open Data Commons Open Database License 1.0
ODbL-1.0.attribution: "© OpenStreetMap contributors" and say the data is available under the ODbL. A database derived from ODbL data must be offered under the ODbL.

Anyone redistributing must also carry: "The organisations in charge of the Copernicus programme by law or by delegation do not incur any liability for any use of the Copernicus WorldDEM-30", and pass these obligations on.

HydroSHEDS-v1.name: HydroSHEDS version 1 License Agreement (WWF)
HydroSHEDS-v1.attribution: A fixed copyright statement (Exhibit B of the agreement) in the product documentation.
HydroSHEDS-v1.concerns: Free for commercial and non-commercial use, but not an open licence in the usual sense: no distribution as a stand-alone product, end users must get a licence at least as protective, the licence can end at WWF's sole discretion, and the licensee must keep records of end users. Probably unsuitable for a free offline library; maintainers to decide.

source.dataset: Province (outer boundary of the Province of Ontario)
source.publisher: Government of Ontario (Office of the Surveyor General, via Ontario GeoHub)
source.method: Layer extent (NAD83) and the min/max of the polygon's vertices requested in EPSG:4326 agree to 0.001°.

bbox.note: The boundary runs through the Great Lakes to the international line; the south edge is in Lake Erie.
bbox.padded_note: west, south, east, north plus or minus 0.15°, rounded outward to 0.01° — the same margin map_sets.state uses for US states.

terrain.dataset: Medium Resolution Digital Elevation Model (MRDEM) – CanElevation Series
terrain.notes: 30 m, whole country. Replaces the Canadian Digital Elevation Model (CDEM), which NRCan says is no longer supported. Files are cloud-optimised for streaming.

terrain.dataset: High Resolution Digital Elevation Model (HRDEM) – CanElevation Series
terrain.notes: Lidar-based, partial coverage. Optional; the US state maps keep terrain tiles to zoom 12, which 30 m already serves.

crops.notes: 30 m crop-type raster, the nearest match to the USDA Cropland Data Layer. Its class list differs from CDL, so tools/build_crops.py would need a class mapping (orchards, vineyards, berries).

buildings.notes: Harmonised footprints from 107 government sources; coverage is where those sources exist.
Same family as the US source in tools/build_buildings.py. The repository was archived on 8 October 2026 (read-only).
As tools/build_osm_heights.py does for the US.

source.dataset: Province of British Columbia – Boundary Terrestrial (GeoPackage)
source.publisher: GeoBC Branch, Government of British Columbia
source.method: Min/max of all 2,781,686 vertices of the multipart polygon, reprojected from BC Albers (EPSG:3005) to EPSG:4326 with pyproj.
source.cross_check: The legal boundary (ABMS_PROVINCE_SP, marked Access Only in the BC catalogue, so not cited as the source) gives the same west, east and north to 0.001°, and a south edge of 48.2248 in the Juan de Fuca Strait, because it includes coastal waters.

bbox.note: Terrestrial boundary: land plus inland waters, with the coast taken from the Freshwater Atlas.
bbox.padded_note: west, south, east, north plus or minus 0.15°, rounded outward to 0.01° — the same margin map_sets.state uses for US states.

source.dataset: Guyana – Subnational Administrative Boundaries (COD-AB), admin level 0
source.publisher: OCHA Field Information Services Section (source: DEVInfo LAC project)
source.method: Shapefile header of guy_admbnd_adm0_2021 (WGS 84); the same box is shown on the HDX page.
source.cross_check: geoBoundaries GUY ADM0 (CC BY 4.0, 544 vertices): -61.3996, 1.1893, -56.4874, 8.5234 — within 0.04° of this box.

bbox.note: This is the boundary as Guyana administers it and as OCHA publishes it.
bbox.padded_note: west, south, east, north plus or minus 0.15°, rounded outward to 0.01° — the same margin map_sets.state uses for US states.

terrain.publisher: European Space Agency / Airbus Defence and Space
terrain.verified: 2026-11-16 (licence PDF); the collection page itself was seen only as a search result
terrain.notes: A surface model (includes trees and buildings), not bare ground; in rainforest, relief and contours will sit on the canopy.

water.notes: Consistent river lines, but see the licence concerns.
No open dam inventory for Guyana was found.

crops.notes: Map attribution: "© ESA WorldCover project 2021 / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by ESA WorldCover consortium". Land-cover classes (cropland, tree cover, mangroves…), not crop types: no open crop-type map for Guyana was found.

buildings.notes: dataset-links.csv (2026-08-13) lists 34 Guyana tiles. The README says CDLA Permissive 2.0; Overture's attribution page lists the same dataset under ODbL. Confirm which applies before building.
Merges OSM, Microsoft, Google Open Buildings and others.

places.dataset: Guyana COD-AB admin levels 1–2 (10 regions, 27 sub-regions) and gazetteer
places.notes: OCHA says admin level 2 cannot be reconciled with its population dataset, and the level-2 type is "currently not known".

addresses.notes: No open address points found. Overture's address sources (checked 2026-11-16) have no Guyana entry. OpenStreetMap addr:* tags are the only candidate; their coverage was not measured.

pois.notes: Mixed sources; most CDLA Permissive 2.0, Foursquare rows Apache 2.0, AllThePlaces CC0.

postal_code.format: 7 digits: region, locality, district, two-digit post office, two-digit sub-locality
postal_code.note: Guyana now has a postcode system. Many third-party address guides still say it has none; they are out of date. How widely the codes are used day to day is not known.

addressing.last_line: Locality, then the 7-digit postcode on its own line, then GUYANA
addressing.notes: UPU examples use a premises or lot and road ("15 Public Road Section B"), a village or sub-locality, and a locality such as "East Coast Demerara". A 7-digit code is not recognised by the five-digit ZIP rule in engine/address_search.py.
